newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian funds push share prices higher.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian funds push share prices higher.

text.p: Local mutual funds helped push Egyptian stock prices up on Sunday but brokers said they would only be sure that the market was truly bullish after the Eid al-Adha feast holidays.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 4.18 points up to 388.98 points on usual turnover of 65.7 million pounds ($19.35 million).
"The market in general is going up, but we cannot say it is an uptrend. The situation will be clear after holidays," said Dalia Sultan of EFG/Hermes.
The market will close for four days from Tuesday to celebrate Eid al-Adha. More holidays will follow, lasting until the beginning of May.
Helwan Portland Cement was the most active share by far with trade worth 12.366 million pounds. The share, however, ended unchanged at 79 pounds.
"Local funds are buying Helwan because the price is very cheap now," Sultan said.
"Maybe somebody is creating a large portfolio," Yasser Darwish of El-Rashad brokerage said. "Despite the big volume, prices do not go up."
The second on the list of most active shares was Egyptian Tora Portland Cement, which had 5.8 million pounds of shares traded. The stock also ended unchanged at 97 pounds.
Amriyah Cement performed well, rising 0.50 pounds to close at 87 pounds. Shares worth 3.9 million pounds were traded.
"Amriyah is in strong demand and no one wants to sell," Sultan said.
"The cement sector is very strong and stable," Darwish said.
Commercial International Bank topped the banking sector, rising 4.13 pounds to 91 when shares worth 3.28 million were traded.
Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries benefited from an announcement of a rights issue and added 5.3 pounds to close at 111.3.

Abu Qir has said it would issue 8,232,760 new shares to increase capital by about 21.8 percent from 151 million pounds ($44.5 million). It offered the share to shareholders at 45 pounds plus an issuance fee of 0.25 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 608.22 points from 592.2 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also increased to 267.29 points from 266.98.
Out of the 82 shares traded, 33 gained, 22 lost and 27 ended unchanged.
